lesson_title: Number Patterns That Add or Multiply
hook_text: Two patterns both start 3, 6. One ends up at 18. The other passes 700. Same start, wildly different end.
clip_script: Pattern one: start at 3, add 3 each time. 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18. Pattern two: start at 3, multiply by 3 each time. 3, 9, 27, 81, 243, 729. Same first number, and the second one is already past 700 while the first is still at 18. How do you tell them apart? Subtract neighbours: same every time means adding. Divide neighbours: same every time means multiplying. Try 3, 6, 12, 24. Subtract: 3, 6, 12, not the same. Divide: 2, 2, 2. It multiplies. Next is 48. Try the money box, 20, 35, 50, 65. Subtract: 15, 15, 15. It adds. Next is 80. Always say where it starts and what it does, because add 15 from 20 and add 15 from 7 are different roads. Subtract to test adding. Divide to test multiplying.
visual_style: Whiteboard two number lines racing, one in steady steps and one leaping further each time; differences written above one sequence and ratios above another.
mood: A race with a surprising winner.
pacing: The race first, the two tests, two worked examples, then the start-and-rule reminder.
